The proportion of As(III) increased through the water flow paths as reducing processes occurred...This study demonstrates that arsenic distribution and speciation in the evaporation ponds were strongly affected by evaporation and redox chemistry."

section: Other Water-Quality Dimensions: Pesticides, Microbes, Trace Elements, and Greenhouse Gases
subsection: Ecological Responses to Subsurface Drainage
claim_paragraph: Drainage reshapes agricultural ecology from soil fauna upward. \textit{Lumbricus terrestris} abundance was typically higher above drains than between them (median counts twice as high, fresh mass five times), so drainage pattern affects population density and should inform sampling design \parencite{Nuutinen2001,Nuutinen2011}. Drainage type is associated with farmland-bird outcomes, with skylark and meadow pipit favouring open-drained over subsurface-drained fields \parencite{Marja2013}, while tile-drainage wetlands carried cumulative pesticide concentrations $4.7$ times higher than reference wetlands (neonicotinoid-dominated), with measurable neurological effects in juvenile amphibians \parencite{Campbell2023}. Subsurface drainage of meadows was a leading cause of decline in semi-aquatic snails \parencite{Dreyfuss2018}. Restored aquatic habitats can benefit: in restored Iowa oxbows, tile drainage had negligible effects on physical or biotic variables, providing promising evidence that multipurpose oxbows can enhance biodiversity without ecological penalty, with outcomes improved by sediment excavation **[CITATION CHECKED: Leberg2024]**. Crucially, management practices often exert clearer effects than tile drainage itself: no-till and diverse rotations altered bulk density, organic matter, and aggregate stability while cover crops and drainage had minimal effect in some settings \parencite{Saha2024,Hermawan1996,Sherbine2023}, and additional practices such as polyacrylamide amendment and anti-weed mesh with drainage provide further quantified nutrient-retention and production benefits \parencite{Jiang2010,GiménezValero2024,GiménezValero2025}.

section: Other Water-Quality Dimensions: Pesticides, Microbes, Trace Elements, and Greenhouse Gases
subsection: Manure-Borne Microbial Contaminants and Resistance Genes
claim_paragraph: Manure and organic amendments introduce fecal microorganisms, resistance genes, hormones, and trace elements that drainage can rapidly route to receiving waters, with application method and soil moisture---rather than manure presence alone---largely governing transport. Curli-producing \textit{E.\ coli} were far more abundant in tile drains from farms that surface-applied manure than one that incorporated it, indicating that application method itself shapes the transported phenotype \parencite{Truhlar2015}. Tillage governs pathogen delivery mainly through macroporosity: zero tillage generally produced higher subsurface flow and greater \textit{E.\ coli} loads than conventional tillage \parencite{Thiagarajan2007,Jenkins2009}. Antecedent soil moisture and water-table position exert first-order control: effluent on wet soil produced drain-flow \textit{E.\ coli} of $10^{5}$--$10^{7}$ per~100~ml versus $\sim10^{4}$ under a greater moisture deficit, and where preferential flow occurred, drainage concentrations approached those of the applied effluent \parencite{Collins2007,Ding2021}. Manure is also a reservoir of antibiotic resistance genes that persist through drained soils into drainage water: shotgun metagenomics identified $320$ unique ARGs, with manure treatment shifting soil and drainage-water resistomes and many manure-derived genes associated with mobile genetic elements in food- and water-borne pathogens \parencite{Smith2019b}. Steroid hormones were detected only transiently and generally did not differ significantly among treatments \parencite{Jenkins2009}. Engineered receiving features can attenuate microbial loads---a constructed wetland reduced nitrate and \textit{E.\ coli} mass loads $67.6\%$ and $63.3\%$ \parencite{Haverstock2017}--- though some wetlands act as net \textit{E.\ coli} exporters \parencite{Stott2023}. Drained soils, bioreactors, and wetlands host distinct, dynamic microbial communities structured by depth and season, and favourable conditions can be engineered to develop effective denitrifier assemblages **[CITATION CHECKED: Schilling2017]**.

section: Agronomic Benefits: Yield, Salinity Reclamation, and Socio-Economics
subsection: Crop yield and agronomic outcomes
claim_paragraph: The proximate mechanism is relief of excess-water stress and restoration of root-zone aeration \parencite{BENNETT1982,DarziNaftchali2014}, with growth-stage sensitivity (cotton flowering and boll formation most sensitive; surface waterlogging worse than subsurface) \parencite{Qian2021}. Improved aeration propagates through physiology---raising emergence, root vigour, chlorophyll, and dry matter in cotton \parencite{Yang2022}, lowering leaf Na$^+$/K$^+$ in sunflower \parencite{Islam2022}, and raising rice nitrogen-use efficiency $16.1\%$ \parencite{DarziNaftchali2022b}. Controlled drainage repeatedly improves irrigation water-use efficiency without yield loss: simple management of existing Egyptian systems improved WUE $15$--$20\%$ \parencite{Wahba2005}, controlled drainage cut applied irrigation $14$--$16\%$ \parencite{Mahmoud2021}, and Chinese buried pipes raised water productivity, highest near $1.4$~m burial \parencite{Liu2025}. Yield response is soil- and weather-specific: only undrained controls show negative rainfall responses, wet years favour narrower spacing and dry years wider \parencite{Rui2024,Kladivko2005,Acharya2019}, and drainage advanced sowing $7$--$8$ days and avoided $29$--$52\%$ harvest population losses in wet years \parencite{Mourtzinis2021,Nelson2011}. The evidence also delineates limits: where surface drainage is adequate, subsurface drainage did not raise grain yield \parencite{Wiersma2010}; medium-textured soils are most responsive while fine and coarse show no clear effect \parencite{Singh2022b}; over-drainage can induce drought **[CITATION CHECKED: Cordeiro2015]**; an optimum water-table depth exists that varies with soil, crop, and permeability \parencite{HOOGHOUDT1952,Bigelow2001}; and installation without maintenance underperforms \parencite{Malota2016}. Adoption is a leading adaptive practice---about three-fourths of surveyed U.S. producers report drained cropland \parencite{Morton2015}, and nearly $90\%$ of Finnish farmers rate subsurface drainage important, ahead of irrigation \parencite{PeltonenSainio2021}.

section: Agronomic Benefits: Yield, Salinity Reclamation, and Socio-Economics
subsection: Salt leaching and reclamation of saline and waterlogged soils
claim_paragraph: Subsurface drainage reliably lowers the water table below the root zone and removes salt from the upper profile, converting saline and waterlogged land into productive cropland, with topsoil salinity reductions commonly $35$--$80\%$ and corresponding yield gains, validated at production scale **[CITATION CHECKED: Derby2024]**. In India, drained-block salinity fell from $7.18$ to $4.62$~dS~m$^{-1}$ (mean $35.7\%$) while undrained soils rose, and yields increased $18.75$--$27.62\%$ \parencite{Sharma2006}; wide-spacing reclamation lowered topsoil salinity from $8.4$ to about $2.1$~dS~m$^{-1}$ and raised cropping intensity from $143\%$ to $191\%$ \parencite{Manjunatha2004}. Chinese reclamations are similarly large: drip-plus-pipe cut EC from about $15$ to $2.9$--$6.9$~dS~m$^{-1}$ and raised seed-cotton yield $52\%$ \parencite{Heng2021}, and after four years the $0$--$1.0$~m layer fell from $27.6$ to $4.1$--$7.2$~dS~m$^{-1}$ \parencite{Zhang2021}. Desalinization is surface-concentrated---$0$--$20$~cm rates exceed $80\%$ while deeper layers lag and the meta-analytic reduction is nonsignificant below $80$~cm \parencite{Han2023,Yang2025}. Comparable reductions are reported for Turkey, Tunisia, and Canada, the last raising barley yield up to twentyfold \parencite{Bahçeci2009,HajAmor2019,Steppuhn2006,Steppuhn2017}, and reclamation homogenises the field and improves porosity and infiltration \parencite{Yu2015,Yu2025,Sharma2000}. Where the water table stays shallow, however, combined waterlogging and salinity are more damaging than waterlogging alone, with yields failing above $12$~dS~m$^{-1}$ \parencite{Kahlown2002}.

section: Agronomic Benefits: Yield, Salinity Reclamation, and Socio-Economics
subsection: Salt leaching and reclamation of saline and waterlogged soils
claim_paragraph: Closer spacing and greater depth shorten the desalinization period and increase salt removal, though depth benefits saturate. A DRAINMOD analysis found salinity fell $55.5\%$ in two years at $20$~m spacing but only $5.9\%$ in five years at $200$~m, a slightly-saline target within a decade requiring spacing below $30$~m \parencite{Chen2025}; the meta-analysis generalises this into climate-specific layouts (spacing $>30$~m and depth $>1.2$~m in humid climates; $10$--$20$~m spacing in arid climates with shallow water tables) \parencite{Yang2025}. Field and column studies identify optima near $15$--$20$~m \parencite{Wang2020,Han2023,Chen2022}, with desalination decaying beyond about $30$~m \parencite{Zhu2025b}. Depth effects are pronounced but bounded---pipes shallower than $1.0$~m are essentially invalid for discharging salt \parencite{Qian2021b}, yet returns diminish beyond about $1.4$~m \parencite{Bahçeci2007,Bahçeci2006}, and an intermediate $0.8$--$1.2$~m depth is often preferred under saline irrigation, saving $10$--$15\%$ water \parencite{Feng2017,Muhammad2021}. Envelope and filter design is a first-order control: the envelope factor dominates pipe material, a double-layer geotextile achieving $>95\%$ salt removal while triple layers clog **[CITATION CHECKED: Elzoghby2021]**. Economic analyses converge on roughly $20$~m spacing at $1.2$~m depth as the maximum-return layout \parencite{Chen2025}.

section: Agronomic Benefits: Yield, Salinity Reclamation, and Socio-Economics
subsection: Crop yield and agronomic outcomes
claim_paragraph: Managed practices deliver benefits beyond free drainage when they retain water for crop use in dry periods---quantified at $8.0\%$ average yield gain across 154 comparisons \parencite{Singh2022b}. claim_paragraph: Because drainage water carries disposal costs and externalities, its economics interact with policy. section: Agronomic Benefits: Yield, Salinity Reclamation, and Socio-Economics
subsection: Saline and brackish water reuse
claim_paragraph: Subsurface drainage enables safe reuse of saline and brackish water where salt balance is maintained by adequate leaching. In China, saline ($6$~g~L$^{-1}$) irrigation matched freshwater wheat yields with continued salinity decline \parencite{Gao2023}, and drainage kept saline irrigation viable up to $6.25$~dS~m$^{-1}$ for maize \parencite{Feng2017} and $8.0$~dS~m$^{-1}$ under cut-soiler drainage \parencite{Neha2022}, with cotton optima at $2$--$4$~g~L$^{-1}$ \parencite{Li2024,Lu2019}. section: Modeling, Measurement, and Mapping of Drainage Systems
subsection: Mapping drainage infrastructure and quantifying extent
claim_paragraph: Because buried networks are frequently undocumented, a substantial body of work establishes that non-invasive remote sensing and near-surface geophysics can detect and map subsurface drainage, with a consistent conclusion that no single method or spectral band is universally superior and that detection depends strongly on soil moisture, soil composition, drain depth and diameter, and survey timing relative to rainfall and field operations \parencite{Carlsen2024,Wienken2024,Koganti2021}. In the largest multi-site assessment (29 sites), UAV visible-color imagery detected drain lines at 48\% of sites, multispectral at 59\%, and thermal infrared (TIR) at 69\%, so acquiring all three bands is best practice \parencite{Allred2020}. TIR is the most consistently effective single band, detecting roughly 60\% of infrastructure even under dry conditions when visible imagery failed, though it exploits apparent temperature differences below 1.0\,\textdegree C, requires careful timing (optimally within 12~h of $\sim$2.5~mm rain and late morning to early afternoon), and can fail under low contrast, where RGB imagery guides interpretation **[CITATION CHECKED: Allred2021]**. Aerial visible and multispectral photography likewise reveals functional drains through soil and vegetation contrasts and has repeatedly exposed systems absent from official registries \parencite{Tlapáková2017}. Ground-penetrating radar senses pipes directly, with 250--1000~MHz antennas effective, antenna orientation interacting strongly with soil moisture, and RTK/GNSS-positioned surveys resolving system type in only four to six hours without dense grids; 3D-GPR succeeds where soil electrical conductivity is low enough to limit attenuation \parencite{Allred2005,Allred2013,Allred2018b,Koganti2020}. Geoelectrical methods coupling time-lapse ERT with injected water or pressurised air locate networks by induced resistivity change \parencite{Jouen2018,Henine2021}. The best-supported strategy is combining methods with complementary sensitivities---particularly UAV RGB/TIR imagery with GPR, which adds pipe depth and orientation---since each has distinct favourable conditions and linear farm features are otherwise easily confused with drain lines \parencite{Koganti2021,Carlsen2024,Wienken2024,Allred2020}.

section: Modeling, Measurement, and Mapping of Drainage Systems
subsection: Analytical drain-spacing solutions and pipe-scale hydraulics
claim_paragraph: Unsteady-state (transient) spacing equations yield markedly narrower spacings than steady-state equations and are preferred under variable rainfall---about 30~m versus 55~m in Iranian paddies---with the appropriate transient model depending on rainfall duration and design criterion \parencite{OOSTERBAAN1988,DarziNaftchally2014,Moshayedi2020,Pali2014,Nédélec2010}. Incorporating evapotranspiration and unsaturated-zone flow generally permits wider, more economical spacing: ET-aware solutions allow 9--18\% increases, bare-soil evaporation 23--74\%, and unsaturated horizontal flow up to 30\% for coarse soils near a shallow impervious layer \parencite{NIKAM1992,Singh2010,Upadhyaya2000,AbdelFattah2005,Yousfi2014}. Bi-level and sloping-aquifer solutions show asymmetric water tables and slightly to moderately larger spacings, and dual-depth systems always remove water more effectively than single-depth ones \parencite{Verma1998,Kankarej2023,Upadhyaya2013,Hartani2001,Kirkham1997}. Analytical solutions for multi-layered and ponded systems have been verified against experiments and MODFLOW, establishing strong three-dimensionality and sensitivity to anisotropy near drains, while flat-land theory remains applicable on slopes up to about $0.15$~m~m$^{-1}$ **[CITATION CHECKED: CHU1977]**; no single linear-diffusion model, however, can describe all stages of drawdown \parencite{Kacimov2000}. The most complete descriptions solve the Richards equation, but corrected Boussinesq approximations remain useful for design when a variable drainable porosity or effective specific yield is used \parencite{TANG1977,Xin2016c,VANDELEUR1959,SINGH1980,Bouarfa2000}. Single-tile solutions using a variable region of influence eliminate the spacing parameter for irregular systems \parencite{Cooke2001}, and space-fractional and inverse formulations improve fits in heterogeneous soils and circumvent the awkward drainable-porosity parameter \parencite{FathAllah2025,Mehdinejadiani2013,Mehdinejadiani2020,Mehdinejadiani2022,Samani2007,Chahar2010,SINGH1992,KUMAR1994,Onyejekwe1999,Bahceci2008}.

section: Modeling, Measurement, and Mapping of Drainage Systems
subsection: Field-scale drainage and water-quality models
claim_paragraph: For water quality the same pattern recurs across the model families (\textsc{DRAINMOD} suite, RZWQM/RZWQM2, SWAT/APEX, APSIM, DNDC, HYDRUS): after calibration they reproduce annual and cumulative drainage and nitrate loss well---frequently within $\pm5$--$20\%$---and capture the direction of management effects, but predictive skill falls with temporal disaggregation, nitrate is predicted less accurately than flow, and daily nitrate concentrations, crop N uptake, and residual soil N are recurrent weak points \parencite{Youssef2018,Negm2014,Singh2020b,Dayyani2010,Ma2001,Liang2018,Ikenberry2017,Marjerison2016,Ojeda2018,Qi2025,Ma2007,Ahuja2007}. \textsc{DRAINMOD-N~II} and RZWQM2 both satisfactorily predict tile nitrate, and \textsc{DRAINMOD-DSSAT} predicts drainage, nitrate, and yield very well \parencite{Du2017,Qi2012,Negm2017,Singh2022c}; cropping-system models (DSSAT, RZWQM, DNDC, APSIM, SWAT) likewise reproduce cover-crop and rotation effects on nitrate loss \parencite{Jeong2018,Ahmed2007b,Ale2012b,Pasley2021,Motarjemi2021}. Phosphorus extensions are advancing but remain limited: RZWQM2-P first simulated daily dissolved reactive P and its pathway partitioning, while \textsc{DRAINMOD-P} predicted discharge and total P but poorly predicted DRP, and few standard models yet represent tile P \parencite{Sadhukhan2019,Grewal2025,BinShokrana2023b,Askar2021,Askar2025,Radcliffe2015,Wang2020b}. Cold-season snowmelt and freeze--thaw errors motivated dedicated developments (\textsc{DRAINMOD}~5.1, DRAIN-WARMF, RZ-SHAW), and calibration studies repeatedly identify lateral saturated conductivity in the tile layer and field capacity as controlling predictions **[CITATION CHECKED: Malone2017]**.

section: Modeling, Measurement, and Mapping of Drainage Systems
subsection: Data-driven, remote-sensing, and geostatistical methods
claim_paragraph: Data-driven methods frequently match or outperform process models for the specific outputs on which they are trained while requiring less data and computation. Neural networks predicted real-time water-table control and saturated conductivity more accurately than pedotransfer functions (the ANN prediction of saturated conductivity reaching $R^2$ up to 0.96), random forests outperformed linear regression for agronomic prediction, and an Attention~U-Net surrogate reached test $R^2$ of 0.997--1 for head, drainage volume, and salt discharge while drastically reducing computation \parencite{Yang2000,Ellafi2021,Djiemon2019,Lei2026,Sarangi2006,Bakhsh2005b,Bakhsh2007b}. Ancillary sensing infers drainage-relevant surface conditions through SAR, Landsat SWIR, and vegetation indices \parencite{Meunier2001,Rijal2013,Xu2018,Khanal2020}. section: Modeling, Measurement, and Mapping of Drainage Systems
subsection: Flow physics: saturated and unsaturated flow and preferential-flow representation
claim_paragraph: A central mechanistic result is that treating drainage as purely saturated flow overstates discharge. A saturated-flow model over-predicted seepage and drainage time by roughly an order of magnitude relative to experiment, an analytical solution, and the SUTRA Richards-equation model, because a vadose zone retaining substantial water persists even at steady state \parencite{Xin2016b}. Saturated--unsaturated drainage is governed by gravitational, pressure, capillary, and air-pressure potentials, so saturated conductivity alone is an inadequate design basis \parencite{Li2021}. Field diagnosis in Japanese paddies showed that vertical, not horizontal, resistance limits the maximum drainage rate \parencite{Nishida2020}, accounting for vertical head loss improved water-table prediction \parencite{Talukolaee2022}, and retaining unsaturated-zone buffering matched numerical models closely whereas ignoring it distorted transients \parencite{VandeCraats2021}; equivalent-medium representations reproduce integrated outflow well but can misrepresent internal dynamics where fast vertical flow occurs \parencite{Carlier2007}. At field-to-hillslope scale the representation of macropores is decisive for reproducing rapid drainage. Dual-permeability and dual-porosity models reproduce hydrographs well ($R^2=0.84$; groundwater $r=0.98$) while single-porosity models reach acceptable accuracy with far fewer parameters, though all fail to match low dry-season discharge \parencite{Varvaris2018}; dual-permeability formulations enable low matrix conductivity while still reproducing fast events **[CITATION CHECKED: Salo2017]**, adding macropore flow improves peak simulation without changing total drainage \parencite{Zhou2013}, and bimodal retention functions predict preferential flow far better than unimodal ones \parencite{Mohanty1997}. Fully coupled surface--subsurface--tile models are recommended for detailed dynamics, with equivalent-porous-medium or seepage-node simplifications reproducing outflow almost exactly for watershed integration \parencite{DeSchepper2015,Boico2022,Xian2017}.

section: Modeling, Measurement, and Mapping of Drainage Systems
subsection: Watershed representation, sensitivity, calibration, uncertainty, and evaluation
claim_paragraph: Formal analyses converge on saturated hydraulic conductivity and evapotranspiration estimation as the dominant sources of sensitivity and uncertainty, with van Genuchten shape parameters, drain spacing, and depth also prominent, and parameter uncertainty propagating into predicted salinity and yield **[CITATION CHECKED: Timalsina2023]**. Objective-function design strongly affects identifiability: genetic algorithms generally outperform PEST, combining discharge with water-table depth already gives excellent results, and variational data assimilation cut a five-year cumulative-volume discrepancy below 1\% \parencite{Sedaghatdoost2019,Chelil2022b,Schoups2005}. The review literature concludes no universal model exists and that automatic calibration is preferable because it supports uncertainty estimation \parencite{Singh2019b}. Measurement protocols matter equally: calibrated V-notch and compound weirs, flow meters, and flow-proportional sampling minimise bias in discharge and load estimates that otherwise propagates into nutrient budgets \parencite{Christianson2019,BinShokrana2021,Napierala2023,Katuwal2024,Enamorado2007,Dialameh2022,Young2023}.
